svg.text: ONE CA bus, time-shared. ACT to rank0 (p0-p1, cs=r0), ACT to rank1 (p2-p3, cs=r1). Not parallel - serialized, CS picks rank.

svg.text: PRE is 1 UI -> fits one phase each. WR (2 UI) + 2 PRE (1 UI) = 4 phases = 3 cmds (tPPD=2 ok @ p2,p3).

text.font-family: JetBrains Mono, DejaVu Sans Mono, monospace
Inter, DejaVu Sans, sans-serif

svg.text: 1. dfi_clk = CK/GEAR (slow). 1:4 -> one dfi_clk edge = 4 CK = 4 CA phases. MC drives dfi_address_p0..p3 + dfi_cs_p0..p3 ALL AT ONCE (parallel wires).

text.font-family: Inter, DejaVu Sans, sans-serif

svg.text: 2. PHY serializes: p0->CK0, p1->CK1, p2->CK2, p3->CK3 onto the ONE DRAM CA bus. Nothing runs 4 commands in parallel - the CA bus is one bus at CK rate.

text.font-family: Inter, DejaVu Sans, sans-serif

svg.text: 3. DDR5 command = 2 UI = 2 CK = 2 phases (ACT/RD/WR); PRE/REF = 1 UI = 1 phase.

text.font-family: Inter, DejaVu Sans, sans-serif

svg.text: 4. 4 phases -> max 2 two-UI cmds ([C C A A]) OR 1 two-UI + 2 one-UI ([C C P P]) = up to 3.

text.font-family: Inter, DejaVu Sans, sans-serif

svg.text: 5. 2 ACT diff-rank = all 4 phases [A A A A]; dfi_cs per phase-pair selects the rank. One CA bus, time-shared, CS routes - that is the ONLY way two ACTs coexist in a bundle.
